name: Alabama
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim. Alabama has no alternate base period.
notModeled: The weeks rise from 14 to as many as 20 when Alabama's average unemployment rate for the most recent third quarter is above 6.5%; the Department put September 2026's at 3.5% (preliminary).
Five more weeks for a claimant in approved training.
A claimant with an earlier benefit year must have earned 8 times the earlier weekly amount since it began.

citation.sourceDocument: Code of Ala. §§25-4-1, 25-4-72, 25-4-74, 25-4-77; Alabama Department of Workforce, Unemployment FAQ
citation.sourceNote: §25-4-72(b): the weekly amount is "one twenty-sixth of the average of the wages" in "the two quarters of his or her base period in which the total wages were the highest", that is half the two-quarter total over 26. Cents "in excess of fifty cents ($.50)" round up, and "fifty cents ($.50) or less shall be dropped". "If the amount derived ... is not in excess of forty-four dollars fifty cents ($44.50), there shall be no weekly benefit amount"; above $274.50 it is "two hundred seventy-five dollars ($275)". §25-4-77(a)(6): base-period wages of "one and one-half times" the high quarter. §25-4-74(a): the total is the lesser of "14 times" the weekly amount at an unemployment rate of 6.5% or less and "one fourth of the wages" in the base period, "computed to the nearest multiple of one dollar". The Department: "maximum in Alabama is $275 a week". No dependent allowance; one unpaid waiting week. Read 2026-10-19.
